key_insight: Aligned clean spherical bubble chains generate a nearly uniform upward liquid flow because their trajectories arrange far wakes so that bubble-induced velocities superpose across the chain.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a reduced-order way to predict bubble-driven liquid circulation, useful for designing and interpreting bubbly flows in reactors, columns, and multiphase process equipment.
method: High-accuracy embedded-boundary simulations resolved bubble boundary layers and long-range bubble-bubble interactions.
Hydrodynamic interaction evolution was quantified to determine when isolated-bubble far wakes can be superposed.
A reduced-order model based on bubble trajectories was validated against experimental measurements.
evidence_signal: The model reproduced the experimentally observed nearly uniform upward liquid flow and distinguished it from a center-peaked profile predicted for a uniformly dispersed bubble arrangement.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate bubble trajectories and clean spherical-bubble assumptions, so performance may change for deforming, contaminated, or strongly turbulent bubbles.
paper_title: Prediction of Spherical Bubble-Chain-Induced Liquid Flow through Far-Wake Superposition Based on Bubble-Chain Hydrodynamics
